entry_points.text: Early boot creates the default root with exempt self state, binds the initial task, assigns indices and names, validates callbacks and names, and brings only early subsystems online with fixed identifiers.

Late boot checks mask width, registers base files, prepares locking, namespaces, reaping and notifications, then initializes each subsystem with identifiers, masks, tables, binding and population, followed by rehashing and registration.

Ordered workqueues serve offline, release and free with per-processor dead-task lists where supported; stats setup allocates per-processor lists when a subsystem is given and always initializes locking and heads.
Boot disable lists filter subsystems; new tasks start in the initial set; deadline teardown decrements placement counts; and a flag-gated helper bumps caller pressure under RCU.

exports.text: Mkdir checks name, liveness and ancestor ceilings then links, populates and activates, destroying on late failure; rmdir needs no tasks and no online children before marking dead, teardown and accounting.

Groups resolve from ids, namespace-relative paths, and file or descriptor handles, rechecking directory nature, liveness and hierarchy under read-side protection and failing on missing, dead or foreign targets.

Membership display walks hierarchies under read-side plus spin protection, skipping hidden or unmounted roots, and prints per-hierarchy attachment with namespace-relative paths, handling exiting tasks per hierarchy type.

Fork pins inherited membership or a live writable directed destination and records kill generation; commit links the child, applies freeze and kill policy and notifies subsystems, while abort drops the same holdings once.

Exit and release forward to registered subsystems; death unlinks the task, maintains counts, parks dying leaders, and refreshes deadline and frozen state, either inline or via a per-processor deferred queue by build.

Sockets bind to the creator default group, fall back to the default root in interrupt context, tolerate cloning from removed groups, and pair every group and filter acquisition with a matching release.

hazards.text: Sibling emptiness cannot prove removability because dead children stay linked; only online status works. Backpointers need read-side dereference, line breaks in names are rejected, and an extra node hold lasts until deferred free.
Distinct failures cover invalid names, dead parents, ceiling exceeded, allocation failure, busy removal, unknown identifiers, namespace escape and oversize paths translated to name-too-long.

Fork and lookup must balance references across all legs and recheck path liveness; kill generation and freeze sampled early are rechecked after linkage, and dying-leader liveness must agree with iteration.

Offline CPUs to the scheduler installer can panic, so rebuild validates subsets and aborts with warning; allocation failures fall back to one default domain; rebind is mutex serialized; and migration always drops mm references.

invariants.text: Live counts grow at commitment and move to dying at destruction with symmetric frozen tracking; non-self release expects zero descendants, and creation fails when any ancestor would exceed depth or breadth ceilings.

Roots are never destroyed, use reserved early identifiers and persistent later ones, and new groups get monotonic serials; init tasks stay unlinked, kernel threads skip freeze and kill policy, and mismatches trap or terminate.

Decimal controls accept an optional fraction, reject malformed or negative-fraction input, and scale with round-to-nearest; numeric identity lookup requires the caller to already hold read-side protection.

Placement derives from subsystem linkage with null tolerance and from task or parent linkage; online needs online and not dying, options test independently, and overlap is effective-CPU intersection with lock-guarded population.

Rebuild needs CPU and cpuset guards, verifies domains lie within active CPUs and aborts with warning otherwise; valid partitions need positive root state, and both generators fall back to one null domain on allocation failure.

CPU refresh intersects task-possible with effective CPUs except restricted top tasks; node refresh uses a rebind marker, guaranteed-online mask and leader-only migration; validation enforces subsets and rejects newly emptying sets.

locks.text: The hierarchy mutex serializes offline, limit checks, destruction, killed draining and release; offline and destroy assert it is held and workers acquire it around critical sections before dropping references.

A spin guard covers descendant, dying and frozen counts plus link liveness with read-side backpointers; membership holds read-side plus spin, and id, path and death paths recheck liveness with retry on racing removal.

Threadgroup protection spans preparation until commit or abort, global protection only for directed placement, sampling uses interrupt-safe set exclusion, and freeze marking nests signal inside set exclusion.

Full order is top mutex, CPUs guard, then cpuset mutex with reverse release; callbacks use an interrupt-disabling spin pair, meters use their spin, and population queries need the placement mutex while skipping offline records.

state_machines.text: Offline work walks toward root with callbacks, flag clear, detach and wake; deferred release marks released, flushes stats and diverges for self versus non-self before freed work, with a finish worker serializing completion.

Lifetime moves from allocation through commitment, then population, enabling and activation, unwinding via locked destruction on late failure; destruction needs quiescence, then disables binding, terminates states, removes the node and notifies offline.

Creation moves through preparation and commitment publishing linkage and policy; hotplug emptying queues a referenced carrier, then the worker migrates tasks to the nearest ancestor with CPUs and memory and frees it.

structs.text: A group carries root linkage, depth, ancestor table, node pointer, self state, descendant totals with dying arrays and ceilings, masks, flags, freezer state and slots; states carry owner pointers, identifiers, counts and deferred work.

Placement holds linkage, option word, CPU and node masks with exclusive views, prior nodes, partition state, deadline accounting and pressure settings; pressure state holds count, value, timestamp and spin; removal pairs work with target.

Rate constants fix decay 933 for about ten seconds half life, tick cap 99, saturation 1000000, and scale 1000; updates decay by whole seconds and fold pending counts weighted by coefficient complement, starting zeroed.

Vocabularies cover partition diagnostics, option toggles for spreading, balancing, migration, hardwall and exclusivity, control identities for pressure, domain, partition and CPU and node views, and capability flags.

At most thirty-two subsystems are supported; system attributes join delegate and capability entries under a common group name, merging base, conditional pressure and per-subsystem delegatable entries.
